summary: Return the k-th largest sum of node values over complete levels, or -1 if fewer than k levels.
mainInsight: Compute each level's sum with a BFS, then pick the k-th largest: keep a min-heap of size k (root = k-th largest) or sort the sums.

approaches.name: BFS + sort the level sums
approaches.summary: Collect sums, sort descending, take index k - 1.

approaches.name: BFS + min-heap of size k
approaches.summary: Push each sum; pop when size > k.

promptVariants: Which structure keeps the k largest level sums?
How do you combine BFS with selection?
options: Compute sums by BFS, then a size-k min-heap (or a sort)
A max-heap holding all of the nodes' values
DFS only, with a running sum per node
A stack of the level sums in visit order
cards.answer: Compute sums by BFS, then a size-k min-heap (or a sort)
cards.explanation: The heap root is the k-th largest sum seen.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A max-heap holding all of the nodes' val: Nodes are not the quantity ranked.
incorrectOptionExplanations.DFS only, with a running sum per node: Level sums are natural with BFS.

promptVariants: Why is the answer -1 when there are fewer than k levels?
How does the heap size reveal that?
cards.answer: There must be at least k level sums to have a k-th largest; if the heap holds fewer than k sums after processing all levels, no k-th exists and -1 is returned.
cards.explanation: Compare len(heap) with k at the end.

promptVariants: Time complexity with L levels (BFS O(n) + heap): ___
Complete the statement: Time complexity with L levels (BFS O(n) + heap): ___
cards.explanation: BFS visits n nodes; each of L sums costs O(log k) on the heap.

promptVariants: What do the queue and the heap cost?
State the memory used by the BFS queue and by the min-heap of level sums.
cards.answer: Queue O(w) for the widest level, heap O(k).
cards.explanation: Sorting all sums would need O(L).

promptVariants: Why does `heap[-k]` work after the loop (len(heap) == k) and what is the clearer expression? What is risky about `if levelSum:`?
cards.answer: At that point the heap has exactly k elements, so heap[-k] is index 0 - the root, the k-th largest. Writing heap[0] is clearer (a heap list is not sorted, so heap[-k] is misleading in general). `if levelSum:` skips levels whose sum is 0, which is only valid because node values are positive; an explicit empty-level check is safer.
keyPoints: Zero-sum skip relies on positive values
cards.explanation: A heap list is not in sorted order.

promptVariants: What is returned when the tree has fewer than k levels?
options: -1, because the heap has fewer than k sums
0, because the missing levels sum to zero
The smallest level sum found in the tree
An error because k exceeds the tree height
cards.answer: -1, because the heap has fewer than k sums
cards.explanation: Only L < k sums exist, so there is no k-th largest.
